skill.name: easy-for-them

skill.summary: Reduce unnecessary steps and prepare messages that people can follow or forward without editing.

content.user_title: Write Clear Instructions People Can Follow
content.value_statement: Long instructions and vague requests make routine tasks harder for clients and teammates. This skill guides assistants to write concise messages with direct links, copy-ready values, and clear completion checks.
actual_capabilities: Identify unnecessary human steps before drafting instructions.
Use observed URLs to prepare direct links and disclose when destinations cannot be verified.
Write numbered actions in plain language for phone screens.
Place copy-ready values separately and prepare messaging links with prefilled text.
Draft client messages in the sender's voice, ready to forward.
Combine requests into one message and explain how to confirm completion.
limitations: Provides writing guidance, not bundled scripts, integrations, or automated message delivery.
Link verification depends on available tools and access to the destination.
References a companion hands-on skill that is not included in the reviewed files.
Does not define safeguards for sharing codes, account details, or screenshots; users must apply their own privacy controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Setup Messages
use_cases.description: Turn setup requirements into a short message with exact links, necessary values, and an explicit completion check.

use_cases.title: Simplify Support Replies
use_cases.description: Rewrite troubleshooting instructions as clear phone-friendly actions and describe the expected result.

use_cases.title: Collect Project Details Together
use_cases.description: Combine outstanding information requests into one message that explains what is needed and how to reply.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Shorten Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite these instructions for someone using a phone: [instructions]. Use plain words, one numbered action per line, and a clear completion check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing set of instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Draft a Client Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a ready-to-forward message for [client] to complete [task]. Use my [tone] and these observed links: [links]. State what success looks like.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a message the sender can forward without editing.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Combine Requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask [recipient] for these non-sensitive details in one short message: [details]. Explain why each is needed and give one simple reply method.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reduce repeated requests for project information.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Review a Complete Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [workflow] using [observed URLs] and [known values]. Identify removable steps within authorized access. Draft remaining human actions, flag unverified links, and specify completion checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Simplify a multi-step handoff while preserving verification and access boundaries.

output_examples.input: Rewrite this reminder for a phone: Open the shared project brief, add your public business name, and let me know.
output_examples.output:
Hi Sam,
1. Open the shared project brief.
2. Enter your public business name under Business name.
3. Reply here when it is saved.
You should see the name in the brief.

output_examples.input: Ask a client for their public website address and preferred meeting day in one message.
output_examples.output:
Hi Alex,
Please reply with:
1. Your public website address, so I can review the current pages.
2. Your preferred meeting day, so I can propose a time.
A reply here is enough.

best_practices: Provide real observed URLs, known values, recipient context, and the intended tone before requesting a draft.
Verify destination links when possible and clearly disclose links that could not be checked.
Review requests for sensitive information and prefer redacted evidence or secure channels when confirmation is necessary.
anti_patterns: Inventing destination URLs or claiming that unverified links were tested.
Adding jargon, long navigation paths, or tasks the assistant can already complete within authorized access.
Requesting passwords, authentication codes, or unredacted account screenshots through ordinary messages.

faq.question: What does this skill help write?
faq.answer: It guides setup instructions, onboarding messages, information requests, and client communications that require a person to act.

faq.question: Does it send messages automatically?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed file provides drafting guidance and contains no message delivery integration.

faq.question: Can it guarantee that direct links work?
faq.answer: No. It asks the assistant to use observed URLs or check destinations, and disclose when verification is unavailable.

faq.question: Must every message have five steps or fewer?
faq.answer: The skill asks for another simplification review when there are more than five steps. It does not impose a strict limit.

faq.question: Is the hands-on companion included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only SKILL.md, which references hands-on without including its instructions.

faq.question: How should sensitive confirmation details be handled?
faq.answer: Use secure channels and request only necessary information. Redact screenshots and never request passwords or authentication codes in ordinary messages.
